newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain buys Caltex's 40 pct refinery stake.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain buys Caltex's 40 pct refinery stake.

text.p: Bahrain on Monday signed an agreement to buy a 40 percent stake held by Caltex, the Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp joint venture, in Bahrain's refinery, the official Gulf News Agency reported.
Bahrain and Caltex in February signed a letter of intent for Caltex to sell its stake in Bahrain Petroleum Company (BAPCO), which runs the refinery, from April 1.
"According to the agreement...the Bahraini government will fully own and market all its oil products from April 1," the agency said.
Bahrain previously held 60 percent in the Sitra oil refinery which has a capacity of 250,000 barrels of oil per day.
The refinery is a major exporter of petroleum products such as middle distillates to Middle East, African, Indian sub-continent and Asian markets.
Caltex will remain the technical services supplier to the oil refinery, built in 1936, Oil and Industry Minister Sheikh Isa bin Ali al-Khalifa said in the statement.
Bahrain and Caltex over the past six years have been studying plans to modernise the refinery to produce higher value products, including lead-free gasoline.
Bahrain, a small independent oil producer, imports around 200,000 bpd of crude from Saudi Arabia for refining. It produces around 40,000 bpd from its own fields.
